integrity.evidence_source: Ruibo Kou, arxiv:2611.19362v1, Definition 1.1 and Proposition 2.5
integrity.main_claim: Two-scale Gaussian population fluctuations and a continuous integrated count limit with exact covariance for the singular Brownian excursion model
integrity.proof_basis: Exact sigma-finite Poisson interval overlap, compensated-Poisson characteristic exponent with vanishing supremum, and uniform second-moment increment tightness
integrity.reproducibility: checker.py; Python standard library; 1017 finite numerical checks passed; these do not independently prove asymptotic assertions

scientific_limitations: For raw instantaneous live-particle counts, only finite-dimensional Gaussian convergence is asserted; infinite live populations occur at a dense exceptional time set.
The continuous functional limit is for centered time-integrated counts, not for the instantaneous count process.
The fractional Brownian tangent pertains to the Gaussian limit at each fixed strictly positive macroscopic time; no joint shrinking-window limit for finite-T counts is claimed.
Broad Poisson-random-measure and queueing limit theorems may yield related or overlapping specializations; no exhaustive historical uniqueness is asserted.
Independent assessment has not been performed.
title: Gaussian population fluctuations and a continuous integrated limit for singular Brownian-excursion births
